name: Traction machine
description: A gearless permanent-magnet motor sits at the head of the shaft and drives the sheave directly. No gearbox means no gear oil, less heat and markedly less noise.

name: Guide rails & brackets
description: Machined steel T-rails hold the car and counterweight on a single vertical plane for the whole travel. Everything else in the shaft is aligned to them.

name: Safety gear & governor
description: An overspeed governor watches the car's descent. If it ever exceeds the trip speed, progressive safety gear grips the rails and stops the car mechanically.

name: Control system
description: A VVVF drive shapes every start and stop, so acceleration is a curve rather than a step. Floor levelling lands within a few millimetres, loaded or empty.

name: Door operator
description: The doors are the part passengers touch most. A dedicated VVVF operator drives them, with a full-height light curtain that reopens on any obstruction.

name: Counterweight
description: Cast filler weights balance the car plus roughly half its rated load, so the motor only ever moves the difference.

name: Suspension ropes
description: Multiple independent steel ropes carry the car, each rated well beyond the whole load. They are inspected and re-tensioned at every service.

name: Pit buffers
description: At the bottom of the shaft, buffers absorb the energy of an over-travel so nothing reaches the pit floor at speed.
detail: Polyurethane or oil buffers, by speed
